So `identify_http_path` returns `end_of_line + 1`, which is the character after `\r` in the request line. Then `parse_headers` starts with `p = buffer + 1` (skipping the `\n`).

So the format is:
```
GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n
Header1: value1\r\n
...
Header33: value33\r\n
\r\n
```

Wait, but `parse_headers` starts with `p = buffer + 1`. The `buffer` passed to it is `end_of_line + 1` from `identify_http_path`. So `buffer` points to the `\n` after the request line, and `p = buffer + 1` points to the first header character.

Actually wait, let me re-read. `end_of_line = memchr(buffer, '\r', ...)` finds the `\r` at the end of the request line. Then `*end_of_line = '\0'` null-terminates the URL. Then `return end_of_line + 1` returns the character after `\r`, which is `\n`.

Then in `parse_headers`, `p = buffer + 1` skips the `\n`, so `p` points to the first header character.

So the format is:
```
GET / HTTP/1.0\r\nHeader1: value1\r\nHeader2: value2\r\n...\r\n\r\n
```
